Rashi on Pesachim 72b:11:1.english: On the porch - In front of the house, like a gatehouse, and they call [it] poria.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:11:2.hebrew: בשפוד של צלי - של קודש הראוי, ואכילת קדשים מצוה, דכתיב (שמות כ״ט:ל״ג) ואכלו אותם אשר כופר וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:11:2.english: With a spit of roasted [meat] - Of a consecrated [offering] that is fit [to be eaten]; and eating consecrated [offerings] is a mitzvah, as it is written (Exodus 29:33): "And they shall eat those [things] with which atonement was made, etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:11:3.hebrew: חייב - דטעה בדבר מצוה ולא עשה מצוה, ונותר חייבים על זדונו כרת ושגגתו חטאת, דכתיב (ויקרא י״ט:ח׳) ואוכליו עונו ישא:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:11:3.english: He is liable - For he erred in a mitzvah matter and did not fulfill a mitzvah, and [for] leftover [sacrificial meat], one is liable to karet for intentional transgression and a sin-offering for unwitting transgression, as it is written (Leviticus 19:8): "And he who eats it shall bear his iniquity."

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:12:1.hebrew: אשתו נדה בעל חייב - כדמוקי לה לקמיה בסמוך לווסתה ובמעוברת, דלאו מצוה היא. ולקמיה מפרש ואזיל אם חלוק הוא על ריש לקיש או מוסיף על דבריו:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:12:1.english: His wife [who was] menstruating, [if] he engaged in intercourse [with her], he is liable - As [the Gemara] establishes it later [as referring to] close to her menstrual period and to a pregnant woman, since it is not a mitzvah. And later [the Gemara] proceeds to explain whether he disagrees with Reish Lakish or adds to his words.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:13:1.english: All the more so in that [case] - [That is, the case of] notar [leftover sacrificial meat].

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:13:2.hebrew: דמחייב - דאין שם לחלוחית מצוה, אבל הכא, אע"ג דמעוברת, מיהו מצות שמחת אשתו איכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:13:2.english: That he is liable - For there is no trace of a mitzvah there; whereas here, even though she is pregnant, there is nevertheless the mitzvah of gladdening his wife.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:14:1.english: In [the case of] a spit - There is no one to ask.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:15:1.hebrew: ור' יוחנן מאי שנא יבמתו - דפטור, ואע"ג דהוה ליה לשיולי:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:15:1.english: And [according to] Rabbi Yochanan, what is different [about] his sister-in-law - That he is exempt, even though he should have asked.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:15:2.hebrew: דקא עביד - מצות יבום, בביאה ראשונה קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:15:2.english: That he is performing - [namely,] the mitzvah of levirate marriage; [the Gemara] is speaking of the first act of intercourse.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:15:3.english: His wife - [He performs] the mitzvah of being fruitful and multiplying.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:16:1.hebrew: עונה - לפי מה שהוא — חמר או גמל או טייל או תלמיד — כדמפרש בכתובות (דף סא:):
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:16:1.english: Conjugal rights - According to what [occupation] he has — a donkey driver, or a camel driver, or a man of leisure, or a [Torah] scholar — as [the Gemara] explains in Ketubot (61b).

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:17:1.hebrew: לשמח את אשתו - אפילו שלא בשעת עונתה, אם רואה שמתאוית לו:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:17:1.english: To gladden his wife - Even not at the time of her conjugal obligation, if he sees that she desires him.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:17:2.hebrew: ומשני בסמוך לווסתה - דמוזהרין ישראל לפרוש מנשותיהן סמוך לזמן ווסת נדותיהן, כדאמרינן בשבועות (דף יח:): והזהרתם את בני ישראל והדוה בנדתה — מכאן אזהרה לבני ישראל שיהו פורשין מנשותיהן כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:17:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Near her expected period - For Israel is warned to separate from their wives near the time of their expected menstrual period, as we say in [Tractate] Shevuot (18b): "And you shall warn the children of Israel... and of her who is unwell in her menstruation" — from here [is derived] a warning to the children of Israel that they should separate from their wives, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:18:1.english: If so, his sister-in-law also - Near her expected menstrual period, the mitzvah [of levirate marriage] is not incumbent upon him.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:18:2.english: [He is] shy of her - [He is] embarrassed before her to ask her whether it is close to her [expected] menstrual period.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:19:1.hebrew: ור' יוחנן - דאמר פטור, כמאן:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:19:1.english: And Rabbi Yochanan - who said [that he is] exempt, in accordance with whom [did he rule]?

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:19:2.english: With permission - [The permission] of a mitzvah with which he was preoccupied.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:20:1.hebrew: דזמנה בהול - שקבוע לה היום, וטרוד ב"אם לא עכשיו אימתי", הולך אצל בקי ללמדו:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:20:1.english: For its time is urgent - For the day is fixed for it, and he is preoccupied with "If not now, when?" [as he] goes to an expert to teach him.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:21:1.hebrew: דזבחים - דפטור במתני' בשוחט לשם פסח, משום דטעה בדבר מצוה ועשה מצוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:21:1.english: With regard to offerings - That he is exempt in our Mishnah when slaughtering [another offering] for the sake of a Paschal offering, because he erred in a matter of a mitzvah and performed a mitzvah.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:21:2.hebrew: זמנו - של פסח בהול הוא היום, למהר פן יעבור זמנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:21:2.english: Its time - [The time] of the Paschal offering is rushed today, [requiring one] to hurry lest its time pass.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:23:1.hebrew: בן גרושה - כהן חלל, זר גמור הוא, דכתיב בכהן הנושא גרושה (ויקרא כא): "לא יחלל זרעו", שמחללו מדין כהונה:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:23:1.english: The son of a divorced woman - A chalal priest is a complete non-priest, as it is written regarding a priest who marries a divorced woman (Leviticus 21[:15]): "He shall not profane his offspring," [meaning] that he profanes him from the status of priesthood.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:23:2.english: Principal and a fifth - For he ate it unwittingly.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:23:3.hebrew: ור' יהושע פוטר - שטעה בדבר מצוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:23:3.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua exempts [him] - For he erred in a matter of a mitzva.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:25:1.english: Because it is called service - [Meaning] eating it, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:25:2.hebrew: ועבודה - של חלל בשוגג רחמנא אכשרה, דתנן כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:25:2.english: And service - [Service] of a chalal [performed] unwittingly, the Merciful One validated it, as we learned [in the Mishnah], etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:26:1.hebrew: ברך ה' חילו - בכהנים כתיב: "ישימו קטורה באפך וגו'", וסמיך ליה: "ברך ה' חילו" — חללים שבו:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:26:1.english: Bless, Lord, his substance - It is written concerning the priests: "They shall place incense before You, etc.," and juxtaposed to it is: "Bless, Lord, his substance [cheilo]" — [referring to] the disqualified priests [chalalim] among them.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:5:1.english: And whether offerings that are not fit - For the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:5:2.hebrew: פטור - הואיל וטרוד במחשבת לבו מאז הופרשו, ויודע שעליו להקריבם, טועה ושוחטן לשם פסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:5:2.english: He is exempt - Since he is preoccupied in the thoughts of his heart from the time they were set aside, and he knows that it is incumbent upon him to offer them, he errs and slaughters them for the sake of a Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:5:3.english: About [offerings] that are not fit, that he is liable - For he is not [considered] one who erred.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:6:1.hebrew: אפילו עגל - דסד"א ליכא דטעי בה:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:6:1.english: Even a calf - For you might have thought [that] no one would err regarding it.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:6:2.hebrew: מודה היה ר' מאיר בבעלי מומין - הואיל ולאו בני קרבן נינהו, לא יכול לומר טועה הוא, וחייב. הכא נמי, חולין לשם פסח יהא חייב, הואיל ולאו בני קרבן נינהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:6:2.english: Rabbi Meir conceded regarding blemished [animals] - Since they are not fit to be sacrificed, he cannot say [that] he is mistaken, and he is liable. Here too, [one who slaughters] non-sacred [animals] for the sake of the Paschal offering should be liable, since they are not fit to be sacrificed.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:6:3.english: He is not preoccupied with them - The thought of sacrificing them is not in his heart until now.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:6:4.hebrew: האי טריד ביה - כל ימי הפרשתן בלבו, ועסוק ואומר: "מתי אפנה ואקריבנו":
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:6:4.english: This [one] he is preoccupied with - All the days of their being set aside, [it is] in his mind, and [he is] occupied and saying, "When will I be free and offer it?"

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:7:1.hebrew: חולין לשם פסח מה לי א"ר מאיר - כלומר, מה ר' מאיר אמר לנו בו:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:7:1.english: Unconsecrated [animals] for the purpose of a Paschal offering, what did Rabbi Meir say to me - That is to say, what did Rabbi Meir say to us regarding it?

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:8:1.hebrew: מודה היה ר' מאיר בבעלי מומין - הואיל ולאו בני קרבן נינהו, לא יכול לומר טועה הוא, וחייב. הכא נמי, חולין לשם פסח יהא חייב, הואיל ולאו בני קרבן נינהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:8:1.english: Rabbi Meir concedes regarding blemished [animals] - Since they are not fit for sacrifice, he cannot say he was mistaken, and he is liable. Here too, [one who slaughters] unconsecrated [animals] for the sake of a Pesach offering should be liable, since they are not fit for sacrifice.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:8:2.hebrew: הני מיחלפי - חולין בקדשים מיחלפי, ויכול לומר: טעיתי, סבור הייתי קדשים הן. משום הכי פטור:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:8:2.english: These can be confused - Unconsecrated [animals] can be confused with consecrated [animals], and he can say: "I erred; I thought they were consecrated [animals]." Therefore, he is exempt.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:8:3.hebrew: הני לא מיחלפי - בעלי מומין בקדשים, לא יכול לומר "טעיתי, כסבור קדשים הן"; משום הכי חייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:8:3.english: These cannot be confused - Blemished [animals] with consecrated [animals]; he cannot say, "I erred, thinking they were consecrated [animals]"; therefore, he is liable.

Rashi on Pesachim 72b:9:1.hebrew: אלמא טעמא משום טירדא - ולאו משום איחלופי, וחולין לא טריד בהקרבתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 72b:9:1.english: It is apparent that the reason is because of preoccupation - and not because of confusion, and [with] non-sacred [animals] he is not preoccupied with their sacrifice.

Tosafot on Pesachim 72b:15:1.hebrew: באשתו נמי קא עביד מצוה - ובסמוך נמי פריך: "והא איכא שמחת עונה". ותימה: הא באשתו נדה קיימינן, דליכא מצוה ולא שמחת עונה! ואומר ר"י דפריך אלישנא בתרא, דפוטר טעה בדבר מצוה אע"פ שלא עשה מצוה; הלכך פריך "והא איכא שמחה", וטעה בדבר מצוה. ומסיק דהוה ליה לשיולי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 72b:15:1.english: With his wife too he is performing a mitzvah - And shortly below [the Gemara] also asks: "But there is the joy of the conjugal obligation!" And [this is] astonishing: surely we are dealing with his menstruating wife [niddah], where there is neither a mitzvah nor the joy of the conjugal obligation! And the Ri says that [the Gemara] asks according to the second version, which exempts one who erred in a mitzvah matter even though he did not [actually] perform a mitzvah; therefore it asks, "But there is joy [of the conjugal obligation]," and he erred in a mitzvah matter. And [the Gemara] concludes that he should have asked [her].

Tosafot on Pesachim 72b:17:1.hebrew: סמוך לווסתה - אין לפרש דיודע שהוא סמוך לווסתה, ומספקא ליה אם נדה גמורה היא אם לאו; דא"כ, ביבמתו אמאי פטור? כיון דיודע שהוא סמוך לווסתה, וסמוך לווסתה דאוריי', דנפקא לן מ"והזהרתם את בני ישראל"! אלא יש לפרש שאינו יודע אם הוא סמוך לווסתה אם לאו, דהוה ליה לשיולה כיון שאינו יודע. והא דאמר בפ"ב דנדה (דף טו.) דכל הנשים בחזקת טהרה לבעליהן — היינו כשיודע שלא הגיע זמן ווסתה, דלא חיישינן שמא שינתה ווסתה. וה"ה דהוה מצי למימר שאינו יודע אם היא נדה גמורה או לאו, אלא נקט דאפילו יודע שאינה נדה, כיון דמספקא ליה אם הוא סמוך לווסתה — באשתו חייב. ומיהו הוה מצי לאשמעינן במספקא ליה אם היא נדה גמורה, ואפי' הכי ביבמתו פטור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 72b:17:1.english: Near her expected date [of menstruation] - One should not explain [this] as [a case] where he knows that it is near her expected date and is in doubt whether she is a full-fledged niddah or not; for if so, why is he exempt [with] his sister-in-law, since he knows that it is near her expected date, and [the prohibition] near her expected date is biblical, as we derive from "And you shall separate the children of Israel"! Rather, one must explain that he does not know whether it is near her expected date or not, so that he should have asked her, since he does not know. And that which [the Gemara] states in the second chapter of Niddah (15a), that all women are in a presumptive state of ritual purity for their husbands — that is when he knows that the time of her expected date has not arrived, for we do not suspect that perhaps her expected date changed. And by the same token, [the Gemara] could have said that he does not know whether she is a full-fledged niddah or not, except that it chose [a stronger case]: that even if he knows she is not a niddah, since he is in doubt whether it is near her expected date — with his wife he is liable. However, it could have taught us [a case] where he is in doubt whether she is a full-fledged niddah, and even so with his sister-in-law he is exempt.
